memo.verdict: Neutral; park. Porr (POS-AT) is a real, slow self-help margin case in a medium-quality Austrian contractor, riding a funded multi-year public infrastructure cycle; at EUR 31.25 (2026-10-08) the 'Modal return' is about 15.0% a year over eighteen months and 11.9% a year over three years, below the 20% bar at both horizons, and the case is not compelling at this price. Two triggers would re-open it: a price below about EUR 29 (EUR 29.3 for the eighteen-month horizon; EUR 25.3 for three years), where the modal eighteen-month return clears 20% a year on the stated path; and the Q3 trading update of 19 November 2026 showing a working-capital release and a Q3 book-to-bill at or above 1.0x, which would raise the odds on the 9.5x re-rating branch. Conviction: medium on the direction of the operating line, low-to-medium on the return, because the return is carried by a multiple the market has just withdrawn. The gate line is not triggered (management C; business quality C with D live; predictability B; trackability C); the case parks on return and riskiness, not on the gate. The record does not invalidate: the direction of the operating line is evidenced and is why the idea is not dropped.
case: - The internal change is one strong force, not many. The cost and selectivity programme (overheads 8.2% of revenue in 2020 to 7.4% in 2025 toward 6.7% in 2030; LEAN mandatory above EUR 20m with over 30% of staff trained; gate reviews on 62% of output; board approval above EUR 100m; "cherry-picking" bidding; materials cost 21.3% of revenue FY2023 to 20.3% FY2025) lifted the EBIT margin from 2.3% FY2023 to 2.6% FY2024 and 3.1% FY2025, FY2025 EBIT +24% on flat output. Standards improvement is the only internal force at B; other leaders, strategy, perimeter, new products and balance sheet are each C; chief-executive change and new geographies are D; price rises are pass-through indexation, not real. Every screen red flag is clear (no caretaker chief executive; not a PowerPoint transformation; no trivial guidance rise; no crown jewels sold; no dangerous leverage; no debt-funded buyback). The internal change is a discipline, not a transformation: it is why the margin case is credible and why it is slow.

- The external force is strong at sector level and has not reached Porr's own revenue. Public civil demand is funded and dated: Austria ÖBB EUR 19.5bn to 2032 and ASFINAG EUR 12.5bn to 2031 (more than EUR 2.0bn in 2026); Poland PKP PLK tenders about EUR 2.7bn in 2026, pipeline EUR 5.5bn, about EUR 230bn to 2030 and beyond, Porr's Polish intake more than doubled to EUR 331m in Q1 2026; Germany EUR 500bn fund, EUR 1.5bn of tenders from October 2026, federal road budget EUR 11bn for 2026, real volume from 2027. It is visible in Strabag's backlog (+27% to EUR 35,985m, 28 Aug 2026) before Porr's top line (revenue -1.1% H1 2026; Q2 intake -32.2%). Direction by force: demand tailwind; competition neutral (top tier selective, third-country bidders excluded in Poland, against Budimex's reports of intense Polish tender pricing, Strabag's acquisitions and CRRC's entry into Austrian rail); disruption neutral; political and regulatory tailwind (German debt-brake relaxation, Infrastructure Future Act, Bau-Turbo, Polish exclusion, RRF 2026 deadline; against it Berlin at least 500 municipal staff short); supply side tailwind on materials and energy (gas 90% hedged to 2030; electricity to 2028; diesel quarterly; over 80% local procurement; EUR 58.8m of materials and services cut in H1) and headwind on labour (German shortage at a level exceeded only at the Covid peak; subcontractor insolvencies rising); own cycle flat; macro mixed (German fiscal pivot for, with civil engineering 58% of revenue and Germany 16% of sales; Austrian GDP growth 0.9% and 0.8% forecasts and eurozone 0.8% against; Poland 3.1% the engine; ECB deposit rate 2.25% in June 2026 after 200 basis points of cuts). The demand force feeds 'Major Corporate Change' as the thing that fills the order book; it is not a 'Demand Inflection' setup because Porr does not capture it disproportionately.

- The outputs have reached the statements and stopped before the estimates. H1 2026 EBIT +15.6% on revenue -1.1%; EPS +34% to EUR 0.71; backlog EUR 9,839m. Consensus EPS 0%, +1%, +1% over one, three and six months; sell-side momentum pinned D. The Q2 EBIT beat of 8% was absorbed because revenue missed consensus by 3.5% and the half-year cash outflow was EUR 257.9m. Of the four key metrics the margin is B (each 10 basis points about EUR 6.5m of EBIT, about 3% of FY2025 EBIT), revenue D (growth falling +11.9% FY2022, +4.5%, +2.3%, +1.7%, -1.1%), cash conversion C (good year-ends, deteriorating half-years, net working capital 11.6% of revenue at Q3 2025 against 6.6% to 9.1%) and net debt C (year-end trend improving on the FactSet basis EUR -207m, -214m, -70.5m at Q4 2023 to 2025; mid-year worse). Sell-side upgrades C: plausible but small and margin-driven; the company is a conservative tracker (FY2025 guided 2.8% to 3.0%, delivered 3.1%; FY2025 EPS EUR 3.00 beat an initial consensus of EUR 2.04), the sell-side explicitly argues the 2030 targets are conservative, but guidance is in line with consensus, our FY2026 EPS of EUR 3.22 sits inside guidance (EBIT about EUR 211m against an implied EUR 205m to EUR 216m), and the revision skew is thin (FY2026 +0.9% over three months, +2.5% over six; FY2027 +0.8%, +1.4%; FY2028 -1.6% over three months on four brokers). Upgrades ahead depend on the year-end cash print and second-half revenue, not on the margin, which is already believed.
counter_case: - At the head of 'Investment Thesis': the stock is cheap because it deserves to be, the "false friend" of the risks research (8 Aug 2026) sharpened by the H1 2026 print. Underneath the record backlog and the year-end cash, Porr is a thin-margin fixed-price contractor whose receivables over 180 days rose to EUR 338.6m in 2025 from EUR 252.4m, about 41% of trade receivables, because clients dispute its claims; whose percentage-of-completion estimates can be unwound by a 0.5-point margin miss costing EUR 36.2m of contract assets on EUR 7.24bn; whose overheads have resisted ten years of programmes (7.4% of revenue against a target set at 6.7%); whose controlling family and chief executive take value through UBM and IGO (related-party flows about 2.4% of revenue against a 0.5% peer median; a EUR 56.4m hybrid subscription chaired by the chief executive on both sides) and through pay (+33% in a year of a margin below peers); and whose owners sold a 4% block near the high. The H1 print is its best evidence: operating cash flow EUR -257.9m against EUR -100.7m; net debt EUR 460.6m; Q2 intake -32%; Germany's output -16.7%; while Strabag grew output 12% and raised FY2026 margin guidance to 5.5% to 6.0%. On this reading the multiple's home is the ten-year median of 7.3x or lower, and the margin story is a slow walk to a level the leader passed years ago. The record concedes most of it: the earnings-quality questions are real; the cash is unproven until 19 November 2026 and March 2027; the governance discount is deserved; the market's refusal to re-rate while estimates held is the crowd telling us something; these are why the case is not progressed. It does not concede the direction of the operating line: three years of margin expansion on cost, an eighteen-month backlog, energy hedged to 2028 and 2030, indexed contracts, no estimate cuts and a dividend covered about three times are not the marks of a business about to disappoint on earnings. Neutral, not bearish. The hypothesis wins if there is no working-capital release on 19 November 2026 or year-end net debt is above EUR 50m: then the cash was not seasonal, the hybrid is not redeemed, and the below-EBIT leg is lost with the multiple.

- At 'Foundations': the foundations are those of a controlled company whose equity is a residual claim behind the syndicate's interests, the margin target reached on paper while cash leaks through UBM and IGO (the EUR 56.4m subscription in a half-year of EUR 257.9m outflow; IGO expenses tripling to TEUR 73,994; pay EUR 2,902k with a EUR 750k special bonus; no clawback; three of eight independent; the chair also chairing nomination and remuneration). Conceded: the related-party frequency is an outlier and the pay record is not shareholders-first; operator quality is C not B for it; it is a 'Case/SP Key Risk'. Not conceded: that the cash leaks at a scale that undoes the thesis; the audit committee is independent, the auditor's opinions clean, the hybrid disclosed at 9%, the dividend risen from EUR 0.50 to EUR 1.05 and paid to all, net cash at end-2023 and end-2025, the new incentive plan tied to the margin; about 2.4% of revenue is a fraction to watch, not one that empties the equity. It wins on a further related-party outlay or block sale (Alarm) or a related-party transaction above EUR 100m (Invalidate).
triggers: - Re-opening triggers (Part 6): a price below about EUR 29 (EUR 29.3 eighteen-month; EUR 25.3 three-year; 52-week low EUR 24.61); the Q3 update of 19 November 2026 showing a working-capital release and a Q3 book-to-bill at or above 1.0x.

- EBIT margin path (Key Driver): modal 3.25% FY2026, 3.45% FY2027, 3.60% FY2028, 3.8% FY2030, probable about 70%; Alarm FY2026 below 3.2%; Invalidate FY2026 at or below 3.0% or any year's margin lower than the prior year's; guidance 3.2% to 3.3%; consensus 3.26%.

- Year-end cash and net cash (Key Driver): modal net cash at or above zero at 31 December 2026, plausible-to-probable about 65%; Alarm no visible working-capital release at the 19 November 2026 update or year-end net debt above EUR 50m; Invalidate year-end net debt above EUR 150m; guidance "net debt free by year-end"; FactSet free cash flow FY2026 EUR 44.9m; one house's net cash EUR 25.8m.

- Public civil order intake (Key Driver): modal FY2026 intake at or above output and backlog above EUR 10bn by mid-2027, probable about 70% for intake matching output, possible about 40% for German volume mattering before 2028; Alarm Q3 book-to-bill below 1.0x with backlog below EUR 9.5bn; Invalidate backlog below EUR 9.0bn.

- Receivables and large-project write-down (Key Risk): possible, high magnitude, rising; Alarm receivables over 180 days up more than 15% at FY2026; Invalidate a write-down above EUR 50m; Brenner Base Tunnel claims unquantified; Leverkusen Bridge dispute unresolved since April 2020.

- Governance and related-party leakage (Key Risk): probable in the sense of continuing, medium magnitude on the multiple, rising; Alarm any further related-party capital outlay or block sale; Invalidate a related-party transaction above EUR 100m.
